releases.title: Backstage Forever 0.2.0 — cinematic desktop and automatic updates

changes.text: From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

Download the Windows x64 setup executable below, run it for your Windows account, then open your existing journal. If you have 0.1.0, install this version manually once: that earlier build has no updater.
Original painted citadel scenery, embossed companion medallion, bronze/leather panels, parchment journal and bundled fantasy typography.

Automatic authenticated update checks/downloads while the app is open. Install on normal exit by default, or choose Restart and update. Preferences and manual checks live in Updates. No forced game-session restart and no external scheduled watcher.

Releases are authenticated by a pinned Ed25519 update key, exact version/repository binding and installer SHA256/size verification. The installer still lacks a Windows publisher certificate; app-update signatures and Windows Authenticode are separate.
Existing local characters, notes, goals, provider connections and privacy defaults are preserved.

Validation: 62 automated tests passed locally, plus real Electron GUI, native storage/reset integration, packaged startup and production-key manifest verification. Wide and compact layouts were inspected. The tag-triggered Windows workflow independently tests/builds/signs this release before publication.

Remaining: actual installed old-to-new self-upgrade/clean-machine acceptance, live ChatGPT/Claude account acceptance, safe Grok subscription inference, account-aware model discovery and verified addon-data import. Grok OAuth exists; inference isolation remains the blocker. The addon is still an experimental template, not certified in-game integration.

Each friend installs independently and uses their own account. No credentials, private signing material or shared backend are bundled. See README, docs/UPDATES.md and docs/ROADMAP.md in the source archive.

releases.title: Backstage Forever 0.3.0 preview — your game-aware companion

changes.text: From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.
Use the Windows x64 setup executable from this repository's Releases page. Existing authenticated updates remain supported; 0.1.0 needs one manual installer upgrade.

Open Game Connection, choose the Forever client folder and install/update the guarded addon with one click. Enable it in the game. Only characters you visit with the addon enabled can become known; there is no account-wide discovery API.

Levelled up or changed areas? Type /reload in WoW to refresh your companion. Logout also saves. The app checks for saved exports every five seconds while open, but WoW writes them only on reload/logout. Visible timestamps describe saved snapshots, not a continuous live feed. The newest account snapshot supplies the last played character. Following starts enabled; deliberately selecting another profile pauses it until you restore its checkbox. Imports preserve notes, goals and unrelated manual profiles.

Model catalogs refresh on startup, connection opening, successful authentication, save and manual refresh. Failed refreshes keep your selection. No paid inference entitlement probes or silent model/provider/billing fallback occur. ChatGPT's account catalog determines visible subscription models; API catalogs and Claude CLI initialization do not guarantee plan entitlement.

Local Ollama remains an offline option with local models. Separate Ollama Cloud uses its own Bearer key and fixed https://ollama.com native chat. ChatGPT subscription access and API billing are separate. Claude subscription uses the official CLI with a private app profile and no API fallback. Grok subscription is still unavailable pending tools/hooks isolation; xAI API mode is available.

The companion permanently assumes World of Warcraft: Forever. A local heuristic handles obvious unrelated questions before provider inference; shared policy guides permitted game questions. This is not a perfect semantic classifier. The app cannot execute code, automate play or provide live combat decisions.

Use my active character now defaults on with a persistent opt-out and preview. Submitted questions may include public name, realm, class, level, race, faction, location and snapshot timestamp. Raw GUIDs, account identifiers, paths, private notes and goals stay out of automatic context. There is no autonomous paid background inference.
Nine original class portraits and Alliance/Horde environments shape the dashboard, roster and journal, with neutral fallback. They are illustrations, not captured player portraits.

Local validation: 120 tests passed, plus real Electron UI, encrypted-storage/game-sync integration, Windows packaging and isolated packaged startup with SDK loading. See Validation and the release workflow for evidence. Real-game acceptance, live OAuth/account entitlement, paid inference and clean-machine/self-upgrade acceptance remain unverified. Ed25519-signed update manifests authenticate installer integrity; Windows Authenticode is still unsigned.

This is a public GitHub preview channel, not an app-store beta/testing track. No release watcher jobs are created. Each player uses their own local copy and credentials. Source is MIT licensed; no credentials or private player snapshots belong in the release.

Set up the companion from first launch or after upgrading. The guided flow discovers the Forever client or offers a folder picker, prepares and verifies its three addon files, repairs missing/outdated owned files, and explains the next action. Enable/load the addon in-game, then voluntarily /reload or log out to save a desktop snapshot.

The local dashboard shows observed quests/objectives, ready turn-ins, available XP, actual game-provided waypoints and up to 25 recent turn-ins observed while tracking. An optional public completed-count is separate from recent history. The draggable/collapsible in-game Adventure Compass updates out of combat and hides during combat. Use /bf show, /bf hide or /bf status.

Desktop imports still check saved files every five seconds and require the game's reload/logout write. This is not a complete historical quest database or optimal route planner. Missing/restricted APIs stay unknown. Race/faction use separate public game readings without a fixed race whitelist.

Provider/model choices save immediately; text settings, notes and encrypted API keys save when you leave the field. Visible save status supports retry, and a secondary Save remains available. Enter submits an explicit AI question; Shift+Enter inserts a line and input-method composition is respected. No AI question runs in the background.

The default-on active-character context has a persistent opt-out and exact preview. It includes bounded public identity, race/faction, quests/objectives, XP, actual destinations and recent observed history. Private journal content, goals, paths, raw GUIDs and account identifiers remain excluded. API billing and subscription access remain separate; Grok subscription is unavailable and xAI API remains available.

Original painted artwork is joined by sculpted controls, gems/runes and ambient motion with reduced-motion and hidden-window handling. Optional schema fields preserve version-1 backups. Stable character form targets and journal merging protect edits during newer imports.

See Validation for measured results. Packaged addon preparation is a release gate because the previous source-only tests missed a shipped-bundle file-access regression. Actual client loading/HUD acceptance, live subscription consent/paid inference, clean-machine install/self-upgrade and Windows Authenticode remain separate gates. Ed25519 update integrity does not sign the Windows publisher identity.

136 automated checks passed, plus real Electron setup/autosave/UI/integration tests. Slow catalog discovery cannot block navigation after a successful save. Independent review verified the export-size and current-folder readiness fixes.
Download availability and final artifacts are established by the public Releases page, not by this feature list. No external release watcher job is created.

Fixes the in-game Adventure Compass remaining at “Waiting for a public character snapshot” despite loading successfully. Lua forwarded multiple class/race/faction API results into a string validator, causing capture to abort. The addon now explicitly uses the first result.

The Compass now uses WoW dialog textures and native close controls, a draggable title, a separate collapse button, content-sized height, and permanent hide/show instructions. Closing prints /bf show in game chat. Position, visibility and collapse preference are saved per character, separately from the desktop snapshot export; fully restart WoW once after this upgrade to ensure the new saved-variable declaration is registered.

After updating the desktop, let it prepare its addon files. In WoW, use /reload to load the corrected script. Once the panel displays your character, use /reload again or log out to flush that first successful snapshot to disk. Subsequent reloads/logout save the current captured state normally. This does not enable continuous disk streaming or gameplay automation.

Regression coverage executes realistic multi-return player APIs in the Lua VM and rejects interpreter errors independently of exit status. All 136 automated tests passed locally. Live verification in Forever confirmed the repaired HUD shows level, class, location, XP and nine observed quests after a player-triggered reload. A subsequent live reload produced a desktop snapshot import, and the updated native-style panel rendered with close/collapse controls, instructions and a moved position; no claim of complete quest API compatibility is made. Windows Authenticode signing remains unavailable; the app-update manifest is separately signed with Ed25519.
A character command center with automatic source-backed quest guidance and a final interface polish using the existing original class/faction artwork.

Your local quest plan rebuilds from imported game snapshots without an AI connection. Choose a session length (15, 30 or 60 minutes) and focus (Balanced, Nearby or Turn-ins); preferences save per character. Session length limits the number of steps shown, rather than inventing completion-time estimates. Inspect why a step was suggested and which saved quest/objectives support it. Explain my plan prepares an AI question for you to review and send; no background inference runs.

This release covers observed quest-log guidance, not a complete quest database. It does not invent prerequisite chains, NPCs, rewards or missing destinations. Game-provided locations are references, not certified shortest travel routes. Stale/missing/manual profiles are identified explicitly. Desktop freshness remains the last saved snapshot, not a continuous live game feed.

Character-specific artwork, roster selection, compact connection/freshness status, XP and quest progress shape the command center. The repeated successful setup banner is removed. Private notes and goals remain local and survive imports.

Optional equipped-item and carried-bag-capacity observations use feature-detected public out-of-combat APIs. Missing/restricted APIs leave those details unknown without blocking identity capture. Preparation data is excluded from automatic provider context. Fixed friendly Compass capture messages replace silent indefinite waiting after a capture failure.

Install the Windows setup executable normally. The companion prepares its updated addon automatically for an already connected game folder. If WoW is running, type /reload to load the updated addon; after it displays your character, use /reload again or log out to save the first updated capture to disk. The desktop imports it automatically. Do not expect clicking Refresh saved snapshot to flush game memory to disk.

Each additional toon must be played once with the addon enabled and exported. Optional Battle.net account roster linking remains research; 0.5 does not ask for account passwords or claim to import every unseen toon. See Guidance and Battle.net research.

The release workflow runs unit, real Electron setup/UI/autosave/integration/command-center tests, builds the installer and checks packaged addon resources before publishing. Exact acceptance results are recorded in Validation. Synthetic fixtures do not certify every Forever API, live provider entitlement or completion of a real installed self-upgrade.
Windows Authenticode publisher signing remains unavailable. App-update downloads have separate pinned Ed25519 signature and SHA256/size verification. No external release watcher jobs are created.

Forever quest references come to your character's plan: reported chain links, NPC locations, listed rewards and better evidence for the next useful step. Local guidance needs no AI account or database setup.
Download the Windows installer · Beginner setup guide

Install the Windows setup executable normally. BF prepares its updated addon for your connected game folder. If WoW is running, type /reload to load the updated addon, then reload again or log out to save its first new capture. BF imports that snapshot automatically. Open Adventure for the enriched plan or Quest Guide to inspect quests.

Quest Guide starts with your character's current quests. Search locally by name or quest ID, inspect chain status, separate guaranteed rewards from reward choices, and review the source build, collection date and report count. Where supported, Copy game waypoint prepares a short /bf guide command for you to paste into WoW. The addon checks it before placing a marker or printing coordinates. You remain in control of all movement and game actions.

The initial licensed pack is bundled for offline use. Compatible game snapshots enable exact-ID/build reference guidance; automatic checks refresh public whole-build data while BF is open. No character details are sent with those downloads. Automatic reference checks can be disabled, and local guidance continues without a provider. Full completed-quest ID sets remain local; explicitly submitted AI questions use only bounded approved reference facts when character sharing is enabled.

The initial pack contains 3,392 server-cache quest records and 1,187 positive reported next-quest links for live Forever build 1.60.1.70862, with smaller observed NPC and objective coverage. A cache record does not prove playability. Reported chain links do not establish all prerequisites. NPC positions are approximate interaction observations. BF shows missing conditions and build conflicts rather than substituting unrelated Classic or beta data. Read coverage and provenance.
Data from Efficient Games (https://efficient.games), licensed under CC BY 4.0, filtered and normalized by Backstage Coding. Application code remains MIT licensed.

The updater now retries temporary connection failures up to three times, uses fresh partial files, preserves older verified installers, and gives clearer retry and Releases actions. Failed newer metadata no longer appears as “up to date.” Signature, repository/version binding, full SHA256 and size verification remain mandatory. Unsafe cache paths and failed partial cleanup stop the operation safely.

If your older BF finds 0.5.0 but cannot download it, download this release's Windows setup executable from the official release page, close BF, and install normally. Your profiles and encrypted connections remain in your Windows account's app-data folder. The old running copy needs a successful upgrade to receive the new updater code. See recovery instructions.

The release gates include unit, Lua, reference-data, real Electron setup/UI/autosave/integration/command-center/Quest Guide and packaged-resource checks. Measured acceptance is recorded in Validation. Public data and synthetic fixtures do not certify every live quest, every Forever API, provider entitlement or completion of an installed self-upgrade. Desktop progress still comes from reload/logout snapshots.

The Windows installer has no Authenticode publisher certificate. App updates use separate pinned Ed25519 signature and installer integrity verification. No gameplay automation, forced reload, paid background inference, external service or scheduled release watcher is added.
Repairs the character-selection and addon capture lifecycle problems found during live 0.6 use.
Download the Windows installer

A saved roster with no active selection now selects its first character consistently. A valid chosen character and the Follow my last played character preference stay intact. The dropdown and dashboard no longer disagree about whether a character is selected.
The addon waits for login to restore its saved roster before capturing a character. Early loading events cannot replace the previous roster before it is read.

Logout preserves the latest prepared snapshot instead of replacing valid XP, objectives and completion history with teardown-time API zeros. Events after logout cannot overwrite it; entering the world refreshes observations again.
The 0.6 quest references, privacy boundaries and signed update verification remain in place.
Opened dropdowns now use explicit dark backgrounds, readable warm text and a clear selection highlight throughout BF, matching the existing fantasy controls while retaining native keyboard behavior.

Close BF and install normally, then reopen it. BF prepares the corrected addon in your connected game folder. In WoW, reload once to load the new addon, then reload again or log out to save a capture made with the repair. Visit the hunter and warrior once each and save after this update; older damaged snapshots need a new observation. Do not delete your characters or reset BF.

A character you have never visited while the addon is enabled cannot be discovered through this snapshot system. Login/capture is necessary once per character. Follow my last played character controls automatic selection; every captured character still stays in the roster when following is off.

Regression tests cover null selection, preserved deliberate selection, pre-login events, two-character roster restoration, logout/postlogout teardown and return to the world. Fixtures do not certify live-client behavior. The installer is not executed during automated acceptance; the player performs installation and reload. Updates remain authenticated with the pinned Ed25519 key; Windows Authenticode signing is separate and is not configured.
Useful quest guidance inside WoW, easier companion preparation and more reliable saved-character switching. The native local planner works without an AI account or the desktop app running.
Download the Windows installer · Living Companion guide

Adventure Compass now builds a compact next-step plan from current public quest observations outside combat. Quest progress, ready turn-ins, XP/levels and supported location events update it without routine reloads. Focus and session controls remember your character's choices. Session size is not a guaranteed completion-time estimate.

Current game titles, objectives and markers take priority. Compatible bundled references can add approximate locations with clear source/relationship labels. A mentioned NPC never becomes an invented finisher, and missing facts stay unknown. The explicit waypoint button identifies its step and source, rechecks the live quest/build guards and places a supported marker or prints coordinates. All movement and game actions remain yours.

The Compass still uses native WoW textures, dragging, close/collapse and per-character positioning. It hides during combat and resumes outside combat. Use /bf show, /bf hide or /bf status. Source and quest-phase labels have reserved space beside the waypoint action, so a long title cannot hide the qualifier.

One primary action discovers and prepares a single validated Forever installation. Several installations produce a choice; no discovery result offers a folder button. Once files are prepared, you can enter BF or play without waiting for an initial desktop capture or connecting AI.

Local running-game awareness helps explain the next step. Open Forever uses only the configured validated executable on your explicit click; ordinary launcher/login use remains available. Unknown runtime status does not block setup. BF does not read game memory, automate authentication, install an OS service or force a reload.

Five managed addon resources are staged and verified, with the loader committed last and bounded application rollback on failure. Unrelated addon files remain untouched. This is not a guarantee of filesystem crash/power-loss atomicity.

BF combines valid primary saved exports from account folders in the connected installation. Per-character timestamps prevent one character's later overall save from suppressing a legitimate update for another. Invalid/transient files preserve good profiles; capacity/omitted coverage is reported. Notes, goals and intentional manual selection stay intact.

Following still applies to saved game data. Re-enabling it can immediately select the current connection's already-known saved active character when freshness guards permit. Characters never visited with the addon enabled cannot be discovered by this system.

Install/restart BF normally and let it prepare the companion. Prepare before launching WoW when possible. If WoW is already running with the addon installed, a voluntary /reload can load the update; otherwise load it on the next game launch. A newly added addon that is not listed may require a game restart.

Once loaded, native guidance updates while you play without routine reloads. Let logout/game exit save naturally for the desktop. If you specifically want fresh desktop or AI context immediately, voluntarily reload to save it. The desktop remains last-saved; it does not have a continuous character feed. Another save after loading an updated addon may be needed to deliver its first new capture, but is not required to use its native guidance.

The bundled native reference is an offline, safely escaped compilation of the existing build-specific Efficient Games pack. Runtime public reference downloads remain validated data; they do not inject executable Lua into the game. Coverage is partial, positions are approximate, and reported links do not establish all prerequisites or a complete travel graph. Data from Efficient Games (https://efficient.games), licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), filtered/compiled by Backstage Coding. Blizzard retains game-content rights; app/addon code remains MIT.

Local plans, setup and browsing make no paid AI requests. Existing provider connections, encrypted credentials and approved-context privacy boundaries remain. Read Privacy, Compatibility and Validation for exact evidence and limits.

Release gates include offline reference reproduction, Lua/runtime and desktop regression checks, independent reviews, rebuilt packaged source/resource byte checks, signed publication and public download authentication. Fixtures do not certify every API in a live client or completion of an installed self-upgrade. The player performs actual installation and in-game acceptance. Windows Authenticode signing remains separate from the pinned Ed25519 application update signature.

Your collected characters and shared plans, together. Company helps you choose a useful character, organize a quest session or dungeon checklist, and recognize new saved quest progress without an AI account.
Download the Windows installer · Adventure Company guide

Open Company for character cards with class/faction presentation, level, last-save labels, ready turn-ins, private goals and available bag/equipment facts. Counts describe collected observations, with unknown data kept distinct from an empty quest log. A suggested character explains the saved facts behind it. Choose its adventure action yourself; browsing Company does not switch your character or change following.
Only characters visited with the addon enabled can be collected. Company uses existing saved profiles; another sign-in is not required.

Create a blank plan or an editable quest-session/dungeon-preparation checklist. Assign steps across characters, leave them unassigned while deciding, or add a quest from a chosen character's saved log. Text edits save on blur; checkboxes and assignments save immediately with visible feedback. Private character journals and existing goals remain intact.

Journeys work locally and are included in deliberate backups. The initial limits are 20 plans with 50 steps each. Removing a character preserves its steps for your review. Converting a tracked quest to another character makes it a manual step instead of silently transferring game evidence.
Templates are your editable planning prompts, not class-role assignments, gear scores or dungeon eligibility verdicts.

changes.section: Quest steps that show their evidence
changes.text: Tracking starts from the selected saved capture. A newer compatible save can prove a new turn-in or a first transition into a known completed-ID list. A ready-to-turn-in quest is not yet a proved turn-in, and disappearance from the log does not prove completion. Repeatables already historically complete require a new observed turn-in; unknown history becoming available is insufficient by itself.

changes.section: Quest steps that show their evidence
changes.text: Manual checks and observed completions have distinct labels. Observed evidence is retained when recent history rolls over, with its build/date qualification. Older saves, changed source identity/build, missing data and orphaned assignments do not become invented progress. Remove/re-add a quest to track another run.

changes.section: Quest steps that show their evidence
changes.text: The desktop still receives normal logout/exit saves. A voluntary reload can save immediately if you specifically need fresh desktop context. There is no routine reload requirement for the live Compass, and tracking does not send an AI request or control gameplay.

Adventure Compass adds a quiet bag-space line when existing supported current observations report two or fewer free slots in a positive bag capacity. It clears when space improves or the session/character changes. Missing or zero capacity is not treated as a full bag.

Native combat hiding, dragging, collapse, close, source-labelled guidance and explicit waypoint controls remain. Use /bf show or /bf hide. The cue has no sound, message or automatic game action, and works with the desktop app closed.

Update/restart BF normally and let it prepare the companion files. Shared plans can use your existing saved characters. Prepare before launching WoW where possible; an already installed addon can load updated files with one voluntary /reload, or on the next game launch. A newly added addon that is not listed may require a game restart.

Native progress updates do not require repeated reloads. Logout/exit saves for the desktop. Your profiles, notes and encrypted provider connections remain; do not reset data to upgrade. Shared journeys stay out of automatic AI context. Anything you deliberately type into an AI question is sent when you submit it.

Old backups without journeys restore an empty shared-plan collection after the existing replacement confirmation. Malformed data preserves current state. Use a current BF version to restore a newer backup.

Release gates cover strict journey migration/bounds, repeatable and unknown-history rules, durable completion, source ownership, privacy, stale responses and reset/import races, normal/Windows-short-path desktop flows, Lua lifecycle/cue geometry, fresh packaged source/five-addon byte checks, signed publication and independent public download verification. Automated tests use synthetic characters and folders. New native rendering/game APIs and actual installation remain player-led acceptance; fixture results do not certify every running-client behavior.

The existing build-specific Efficient Games reference remains partial and source-labelled. Data from Efficient Games (https://efficient.games), licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), filtered/compiled by Backstage Coding; Blizzard retains game-content rights. App/addon code remains MIT. Windows publisher signing remains separate from pinned Ed25519 update integrity.
Privacy · Compatibility · Validation · Roadmap
From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

This checkpoint includes repaired fixture completion and selection preparation, with original focus, caret, chain and held-control assertions preserved. The 0.12.0, 0.12.1 and 0.12.2 candidate tags remain unchanged; none of those app releases was published. This combined preview delivers the 0.9–0.12 development series in one update. Version 1.0 remains held for Frank's hands-on review.
Adventure Director: one explained next quest action, up to two alternatives and one-click tracked Company sessions. Session length limits plan size; it is not a promised completion time.

Preparation: observed professions, learned recipes, dated carried materials and deliberate manual shopping checklists. Complete and partial observations remain distinct; other characters are kept separate.

Optional local voice: hold to create an editable draft, release and review before Send. Explicit local answer/plan reading and Stop are separate. Typed input remains available when engines or permissions are unavailable.

Private character memory: review and save an exchange deliberately. Select specific saved exchanges separately for each future question and inspect the preview. Backups exclude memory; replacement import/reset clears it.

Party: choose your role and create a manual dungeon checklist. Preview/edit every portable line before export or explicit import. Imported plans receive new local IDs and unchecked, unassigned manual steps without completion proof. Sharing stays under your control.

The illustrated class/faction atlas brings selected quests, reported chain links, observed rewards and source-qualified destinations into one dossier. Named-NPC clues remain visibly unconfirmed, even when a historical NPC coordinate exists. Reported links do not prove prerequisites or eligibility. Missing information stays unknown.

The compatible Efficient Games snapshot advances to immutable commit 23f9636486d3d60479dc0bcee2356053c33faf2c, with observations through November 9, 2026 for Forever 1.60.1.70862/enUS. It contains 3,884 cache records and 379 quests with played evidence. Matching-build synthetic reference checks increased coordinate-qualified turn-in destinations 163→301 and unfinished-quest destinations 81→129. Clues are counted separately; coverage remains partial. See definitions, provenance and limits.

The addon adds guarded map-specific and unambiguous in-progress quest-area fallbacks, preserving valid direct points first. A quest area is explicitly labelled as an area rather than an exact NPC/spawn. Missing/restricted optional APIs leave core character/quest/XP capture useful. A newer compatible bundled observation date also takes precedence over an older cache after upgrade, without requiring a manual reference refresh.

A separate historical supply catalog includes 91 listing vendors, 1,301 listing rows and 487 item IDs. Suggestions retain build/faction evidence, collection dates and approximate interaction positions. Current stock, price and access are unverified. Missing Alliance reaction evidence stays unknown; mobile multiple-map history is browse-only. Ask about this supply plan opens an editable question from the selected visible facts; Send remains separate and your character-sharing preference stays unchanged.

Use Updates to check the official Windows preview, then restart when ready. If an older installation cannot download it, close BF and get the Windows setup executable from the official release. The Source ZIP is for developers; normal installation does not need Node.js.

Let BF prepare/verify its five companion files. Load the updated addon on the next game launch, or use one voluntary /reload if WoW is already running. Native guidance updates outside combat without routine reloads. The desktop receives changes when WoW saves on logout/game exit or optional UI reload. Only characters visited with the addon enabled can be known.

App-update downloads use the existing pinned Ed25519 manifest and installer size/hash checks. Windows publisher signing is separate and remains pending. Gameplay inputs, movement, purchases, crafting and sharing remain deliberate player actions. No always-on recording, automatic AI question or new party service is introduced.

Follow Getting started, Privacy and the owner check before 1.0. Validation records automated evidence; real client behavior, microphone quality, installed update recovery and the final 1.0 decision remain player-led checks.
From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

The 0.13.0–0.13.3 candidates were not published; their tags, notes and evidence are preserved. The 0.13.3 candidate passed voice validation, then exposed a travel-smoke assumption about history counts across a deliberate sharing reset. This 0.13.4 patch corrects that fixture and the remaining concrete validation blockers while preparing the same reviewed features for the normal installed Windows update channel. 1.0 remains held for Frank's hands-on acceptance. Earlier local review bundles remain unchanged.

Travel acceptance now acknowledges the exact new main request, terminal result, renderer generation and current painted prompt/response instead of assuming history always grows. Support acceptance follows the current Adventure / Next step breadcrumb. All remaining source validation commands through character guidance were audited in this patch wave.

Party's navigation and setup chrome now use less compact-screen space, keeping the manual checklist action inside the actual 984×635 viewport while retaining its artwork and role controls. Narrow native 200% layouts keep the character identity readable and actions reachable by scrolling. No game action, AI request or sharing behavior changes.

Existing privacy, cancellation, trust and ownership assertions remain. Dependencies, reference data, schemas, protocols and signing trust are unchanged. Prior voice/Map/recovery/gathering corrections remain. No forced restart or intermediate installation is needed.

Proactive Compass: one local recommendation and up to two alternatives for bags, observed quests, qualified learned recipes or profession training. Adventure, Quests and Professions change its priorities. Native guidance uses permitted current events; the desktop says Last saved and No AI. Unknown or partial supply cannot claim craft readiness, skill-ups or guaranteed output.

Quiet native controls: Not now dismisses the current recommendation until relevant facts change. Quest details opens the existing focus/session controls. Hide, collapse, drag and manual supported waypoints remain available. The desktop and native goal preferences are independent.

One Professions workshop: Adventure → Professions combines observed skills, learned recipes, carried materials and deliberate supply plans. Historical acquisition references remain visibly qualified; no bank/alt pooling, invented trainers, rank requirements or prices.

Map in both views: open the game's map normally for BF Layers, historical material references and narrowly supported private finds. Adventure → Map shows last-saved coordinates, quests, historical standing points and your saved observations. It is a coordinate view, without terrain, automatic routes or active-resource claims.

The five main sections are Adventure, Quests, Companion, Characters and Plans. Settings holds Game connection, AI connection and Updates; Help → Field guide holds recovery, backups and support. Existing destinations and class/faction artwork remain. Conversations retain reviewed drafts, cancellation and context boundaries. Local sourced travel can offer conditional route cards and manual trip plans without a provider. Optional voice and saved memory remain deliberate, with per-question sharing choices.

Local diagnostics expose an allowlisted preview before copy/save. Bounded recovery checkpoints and damaged-journal recovery retain their disclosed privacy and deletion rules. No diagnostic upload, automatic AI question, paid fallback, new shared backend or new sharing consent is introduced. See Privacy and Support and recovery.

The acquisition subset contains seven selected relations and seventeen approximate historical player-standing points for build 1.60.1.70862, from pinned November 9 observations. A 1.60.1.70888 character can browse those points only as older references. Native coverage is narrower than desktop seller browsing. Faction access, current availability, stock, skill/rank requirements and exact spawns remain unknown unless separately established. Private finds are past interactions, never active nodes or quantities collected. Supplementary quest notes and travel references retain separate provenance, licenses and coverage limits. No reference pack, game build, dependency, capture schema or protocol changes in this delivery step.

Once this release is published, open Updates → Check now in installed 0.12.3, then choose when to install. Existing automatic download and install-on-exit preferences still apply; BF adds no forced restart. If needed, use the Windows setup executable from the official 0.13.4 release. Source.zip is for developers.

Setup/repair verifies twelve owned addon files: TOC, Reference, Plan, Coach, Acquisition, Profession, Gathering, MapPlan, Map Lua, Map XML, capture and HUD. Unrelated files survive. Load updated files on the next game launch or a voluntary reload; file preparation alone does not prove live addon loading. The desktop receives changes when the game saves normally. Only characters visited with the addon enabled are known.

App-update authenticity uses the existing pinned Ed25519 manifest plus installer size/hash checks. Windows Authenticode publisher signing remains separate and pending. This release uses the existing public preview channel, without watcher jobs.

Automated source, Lua and synthetic GUI evidence does not certify the live client. Current-client Compass/Map rendering, zoom, gathering, interaction and performance; real provider entitlement/billing; microphone and playback quality; screen-reader behavior; clean-machine install/uninstall; and an actual installed self-upgrade remain separate checks. Public publication and authenticated downloaded assets are also verified separately from source preparation. 1.0 remains held until the owner reviews the real experience.
From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

This preview candidate corrects how the packaged Windows acceptance check shuts down and removes its disposable test copy. It carries forward the reviewed NPC guidance, honest current-location context, saved-character previews and connection timing work. 1.0 remains held for Frank's hands-on acceptance. Source preparation, Windows validation, publication and authenticated delivery remain separate gates.

changes.section: Finish the test before reporting success

changes.section: The AI looks things up instead of guessing
changes.text: The lookups cannot act in the game, reach the internet, read files or see notes, goals or memory. Each question allows at most 10 lookups. They work with the OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI APIs, Ollama and Ollama Cloud, the ChatGPT plan and the Claude subscription; the Claude subscription uses only an in-process lookup server, with no Claude Code tools. Larger models (about 27B and up, or cloud models) use the results most reliably.

Turn it on under Settings → Game connection, then type /bf live on once in WoW. The addon draws a tiny calibrated colour strip in the top-left corner of the game window. Backstage Forever reads only that strip, about twice a second, so the companion knows your live:
zone and coordinates, and which way you face
level, XP and free bag space
target NPC
tracked quest and which of its objectives are done
mounted, resting and in-instance state
During combat the strip carries only an "in combat" flag. Values the client protects, such as health, are reported as unknown.

The link sends no input, reads no game memory or files, stores no screenshots and makes no network requests. The Companion panel shows Live · Zone x, y, and AI answers prefer the live position over the last saved snapshot. Stale readings are never presented as live. /bf live status prints an in-game diagnostic, and /bf live off stops the strip.
This was checked in the real Forever client on a 3440×1440 display. Position, facing, level, mount, XP, bags and tracked quest decoded live while flying from Thunder Bluff into the Barrens.

releases.title: Backstage Forever 0.15.0 — find anything, see where you are

changes.text: From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.
This preview is about finding things and seeing them, on your desktop and inside WoW. 1.0 remains held for Frank's hands-on acceptance.
A new World Map in the main navigation draws each zone as an original cartographer's map: parchment, grid, compass rose and town plates in a gilded frame. On top of it:

Your live arrow with facing, a breadcrumb trail, and remembered paths, so the map fills in as you ride. The map follows your live zone when the live link is on, and shows your last saved spot otherwise.

Pins for quest turn-ins, objectives and quests you could pick up (filtered to your level and faction), flight masters, trainers, vendors, herbs, ore and your own recorded gathering finds. Busy areas cluster; click a cluster to zoom.
Near you: the closest useful places with direction ("southwest, short ride").
Find: search every zone for an NPC, "flight master", "trainer", a vendor's wares, "herb" or "ore", nearest first.
Copy waypoint for WoW on any pin. It copies /bf way MapID X Y Name; paste it in chat to get a native waypoint and the game's own arrow.

/bf find Cairne, /bf find flight master, /bf find trainer, /bf find peacebloom and similar commands work with the desktop closed. They search a compiled, source-labelled table of about 900 places, prefer your current zone and the nearest point, set a waypoint, and list alternatives with ready /bf way commands. /bf way MapID X Y [name] sets any waypoint directly.

Adventure → Dungeons & raids lists every classic dungeon and raid with its level band, zone, approximate entrance, boss roster, group roles and preparation checklist. Cards are coloured like in-game difficulty for your level, and your active quests are linked by their bosses; for example, Hidden Enemies appears under Ragefire Chasm. Bosses observed being killed in Forever are marked, and New in Forever shows instances seen in Forever that the classic list doesn't include. Each card can copy its entrance waypoint or open it on the World Map.
The baseline comes from the original game era and is labelled "verify in Forever". Observed Forever encounters are bundled community data (Efficient Games, CC BY 4.0).

From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

Pop-out radar. On the World Map, choose ◉ or Track on radar on any pin. A small, draggable, always-on-top window shows a north-up radar around your live position: your arrow, nearby quest markers, flight masters, trainers, vendors and herb and ore spots, plus town labels. Your tracked target shows as a ring, or as a gold arrow on the rim when it's out of range, with its direction and distance band underneath. Zoom in and out with − and +. Details pause during combat.

The radar only displays. It never sends input to the game. It has its own isolated window and messaging, and it needs the live game link to be on. Over WoW it appears in windowed or borderless fullscreen, not exclusive fullscreen.

changes.text: From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

Pins you can tell apart. Each kind of place has its own shape and colour. Quests are shields: ! to pick up, ? to hand in. Objectives are red crosshairs and flight masters are blue diamonds. Trainers are hexagons: red with swords for class trainers, teal with a hammer for profession trainers. Vendors are coin squares, herbs are leaves, ore is rock, and your own finds carry a star. The layer list, search results, "Near you" and the details card all use the same icons.
NPCs that tell you something. Click an NPC and the card shows:
who they are and which faction they serve
the quests they give and take, marked for you: ready to hand in, in your log, available, level too low, or done
for a class trainer, what you can learn now and later, or that they teach a different class

Do this next: hand in finished quests at the nearest NPC, train new class skills (and where), continue your nearest quest with the next objective, or head to the zone that fits you best.

Quest progress on enemies. Hover an enemy and its tooltip says if it counts for one of your quests, and how far along you are ("Raptor Thieves: Raptor Head 3/12"). Drops count once you've looted that item from that kind of enemy.
You are here. Now opens its side column with a painted card for the zone you're in:
its level range and whether it fits you
how many quests there are for your level, and where most of them start
the inn, the flight master and your class trainer
repair vendors and profession trainers
any elite or higher-level enemies to be careful of
Every row has a Show on map button that opens the map right on that spot.
Zone arrival banners. When you ride into a new zone, a painted banner sweeps in with its name, level range and quests for your level, both in the app and in the game.

Painted map pins. The World Map's quest givers, hand-ins, flight masters, trainers, vendors, herbs, ore and dungeons are now painted medallions, original art made for Backstage Forever. Orgrimmar and Stormwind get their own painted city banners.

releases.title: Backstage Forever 0.27.0 — free AI for everyone

changes.text: From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.
Turn on free AI, in one click. The Companion page has a new Free AI companion card. Click Turn on free AI and the app downloads a small AI model that suits your PC and runs it on your own computer:
The standard model is Qwen3 4B, about 2.3 GB; the light model, Qwen2.5 1.5B, is about 1 GB.
A progress bar shows the download, and Pause lets you stop and pick up later where you left off.

Every download is checked against a fixed fingerprint before it's used.
It uses your graphics card when it can and your processor when it can't.
Remove gives the disk space back.

Or use a free cloud key. On a slower PC, open "Slow PC? Use a free cloud key instead". Click Get a free key for Google Gemini or Groq, paste it, and the app picks a good model for you. Free cloud keys come with daily limits, and Google may use free-tier questions to improve its products.
Upcoming training. Now's training card shows your next three training levels and what each brings, with each spell's icon from your own game install.
Supplies and class helpers in game.
Ammo: warns when arrows or bullets run low.
Food and drink: warns when you're running out.
Pets: tells you when your pet is unhappy.

Each reminder pops up once, when the problem starts. /bf supplies shows everything at once, and /bf supplies off silences the reminders.
Living headers. The Now header slowly drifts across its painted scene, with embers rising, and zone banners pan gently. They stay still if Windows is set to reduce motion.
After updating: type /reload in WoW once so the game loads the new addon file.

Characters → Journey. A new page for each character:
Badge wall: 20 original painted badges:
Quests: 25, 100 and 500 completed.

Speed splits: how much play time each level took, from your own /played. Your best times are in gold, with a marker for your fastest character at that level.

Hover cards everywhere. Rest your mouse on any quest in the app (on Now, in your quest log, in lists) and a card pops up with:
its level
how to do it
who gives it
the rewards, with their icons
Click it to open the full quest as before.
What killed you? After a death, a short review pops up in game:
the enemy that did most of the damage, and how much of it
that enemy's level, and whether it was elite
one plain tip for next time, like "pull one at a time", "that was 3 levels above you" or "move out of that spell"
Session stats. /bf stats shows your fights this session: damage, healing, average damage per second, your best fight and your last one. It reads only your own combat log.

releases.title: Backstage Forever 0.30.0 — loot, crafts and every node you've found

changes.text: From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.
Dungeon loot browser. Instance Atlas → Loot on any dungeon card shows each boss's recorded drops:
item icons with quality colours, slot and drop chance
an Upgrade for you badge, worked out against the gear your character wears
a star to put an item on your wish list; starred items show on the dungeon card
a "3 upgrades for you" chip on each dungeon card

Hover cards for items and NPCs. Rest the mouse on an item (loot, quest rewards, vendor wares) for its stats, whether it's an upgrade and which boss drops it. Rest on an NPC (World Map lists, Now's trainer) for who they are, what they teach or sell, and where they stand.
Professions that guide you.

Best next recipe: the one most likely to give a skill point that you can make soonest.

releases.title: Backstage Forever 0.30.1 — no more "blocked action" notice

releases.title: Backstage Forever 0.31.0 — every page earns its place

changes.text: From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

One look, everywhere. Every page now opens with its own painted banner (twelve new paintings) and uses the same parchment cards as Now. Quests, Professions, Plans, Party, Characters and Dungeons moved over from the older dark styles, and the Companion has its own owl crest.

The dungeon card opens Dungeons, the profession card opens Professions, and the saved-location card opens the World Map on that zone, with the zone's own painting.

Real information instead of filler. Repeated disclaimers became one small "Community data · may differ in game" note, marketing lines are gone, trainers show their zone instead of source counts, and Help → Field guide is rewritten as how-to steps.
One set of class art on every page.

releases.title: Backstage Forever 0.32.0 — a quiet live link

changes.text: From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.
The live strip is now tiny. The coloured strip the addon draws for the app shrinks from 456×12 to 84×4 pixels, about a sixteenth of the space, and it still updates five times a second.
Calibrated colours: four grey reference cells let the app read 4 shades per colour instead of 2, so the same information fits in far fewer cells.
Exact pixels: each cell is exactly 2 screen pixels at any UI scale.
Your corner: /bf live pos topleft|topright|bottomleft|bottomright. The app finds it in whichever corner you pick.
Quiet when idle: after a few seconds of standing still it updates less often, and the app still knows the link is live.

Playing over remote desktop? If the link drops, type /bf live safe to switch back to the larger, sturdier strip; /bf live compact switches back. Settings → Game connection and the Now checklist show which mode and corner are in use.
After updating: type /reload in WoW once.
From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

0.33 also brings the quiet live link from 0.32 (whose installer build didn't finish): the strip the addon draws shrinks from 456×12 to 84×4 pixels, sits in any corner (/bf live pos), and has a sturdy safe mode for remote desktop (/bf live safe).
The app now reacts to what happens in your game, with a painted medallion for each moment:
Death screen: what killed you, its level and whether it was elite, how much of the damage it did, what to change next time, and how to get back to your body.
Boss, elite and rare kills. Killing a dungeon's last boss shows Dungeon cleared.
Profession milestones: every 25 skill points, and when you hit your rank's cap, which rank comes next and where to train it.
New zone, flight path learned, an upgrade equipped, a quest chain finished.
Moments show one at a time, never over the level-up celebration, and a Recent moments card on Now keeps the last few. Turn them off, or just some kinds, in Settings → Game connection.
In game: /bf moments on|off controls quiet toasts for kills and profession milestones. They wait until combat ends.
After updating: type /reload in WoW once.
From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.
Players now help each other find things. When you gather an herb, mine ore, open a chest or meet an NPC, the app can share *where* it was, so everyone's World Map fills in faster.

What is shared: the thing found (herb, ore, chest or NPC id), the zone, and a position rounded to a coarse grid. Nothing else: no character names, no realm, no account, no chat and no IP address is kept. Your install has a random id, and the server only stores a hash of it.

What you get back: once a day, one small download of finds that at least three different players agree on. They show on the World Map, on NPC cards and in the loot browser, marked as community finds. Everything you found yourself still works offline, as before.
Your choice: sharing is on by default. Turn it off, or erase what you sent, in Settings → Community.
Report a problem: Settings → Community → Report a problem shows you exactly what will be sent before you send it.
The service runs on Backstage Coding's own server at bf.backstagecoding.com, with no paid services. Until it's reachable, the app simply waits and tries again later; nothing else changes.
After updating: type /reload in WoW once.
From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

A new Ledger section keeps track of everything your characters own, so you no longer log in to each one to check:

Those prices show here, and on item hover cards across the app, with how old they are. The addon only reads pages you open; it never searches, bids or posts.

In game: /bf ledger shows gold across your characters and when this character's bank and mailbox were last seen. /bf prices on|off|status controls price memory.

A character sheet in the app (Characters → Sheet):
Your equipped gear slot by slot, in quality colours, with item cards on hover and your average item level.
Empty slots, pieces that have fallen behind your level, and upgrades you already own in your bags or bank.
Your base stats, armor, attack power, health and mana, and resistances.

releases.title: Backstage Forever 0.38.0 — ask from the game, a hidden live link

changes.text: From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

Ask the companion without leaving WoW. A new owl button on the edge of your minimap (drag it anywhere around the edge) opens a question box. Type up to 200 characters and press Ask, or type /bf ask in chat. The answer appears in a small panel over the top-right of your game. It never takes the keyboard away from WoW and closes by itself. "Where is…" and "how do I get to…" questions are answered instantly from the built-in reference; anything else goes to the AI you chose in the app. Nothing is sent until you press Ask, and nothing during combat. /bf ask hide hides the button. Your questions and answers also appear in the app's Companion conversation. The panel works over WoW in windowed or "fullscreen (windowed)" mode, not exclusive fullscreen.

A live link you can barely see. The colour strip is gone. releases.title: Backstage Forever 0.38.1 — talents the companion actually knows

changes.text: From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

The companion knows WoW Forever's talents. Until now it was never given any talent data, so the AI guessed from other versions of the game and could invent talents that don't exist here. Now, when you ask about talents, specs or builds, it gets your class's real talent trees, read from your own WoW Forever install: every talent, its maximum rank, which tier it sits in and how many points that tier needs, plus your points at your level. It's told to answer only from that and to say so when something isn't there.

Common questions are answered instantly, with no AI and nothing sent anywhere: "what does Improved Renew do", "what talents should I take", "the first 7 Holy talents", "how many talent points at level 30". If the companion can't tell your class (character sharing off and no class named), it asks.
Also fixed: a remark like "Improved Renew only goes to 3/3" was mistaken for a travel question.

Owl fixes. The answer panel over the game now closes when you click its ✕ (before, a click there could grab the panel to drag it instead). Only the crest and title move the panel, and a panel can no longer get stuck open: if the game takes the mouse back while it's over the panel, the panel notices within a second and closes on time as usual. In the owl's question box, the status and your recent questions no longer write over each other: each sits under the one above, long questions are shortened, and the box grows to fit.

Everyone moves to the hidden live line. If you had chosen the safe or compact strip before, you now start on the thin dark line too, once, with a chat note. If the app says it can't read it (remote desktop, colour filters), type /bf live safe. That choice now sticks.
Community sharing recovers faster. After failed connection attempts the app now waits at most an hour (it was up to six), and turning sharing on in Settings → Community retries straight away.
After updating: type /reload in WoW once.
From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

Every message in game is painted now. The see-through black boxes are gone. Each message Backstage Forever shows you in WoW is a solid painted banner like the zone banners: its own original painting, a gold frame, the title in gold and the text on a dark ribbon.
There are 14 paintings, one for each kind of message:
flight master nearby
quest complete
level up (the big banner)
you died
run back to your body
back on your feet
gear wearing out or broken
move your Hearthstone
Backstage Forever is ready
supplies (food, ammo, pet, soul shards, poisons)
journey firsts
"What happened" after a death
elite, rare and boss kills
profession milestones
Longer messages make the box taller instead of spilling out of it, and the painting is cropped to fit, never stretched.
Nothing else changes: same place on screen, same fade, still quiet in combat, and /bf toasts still turns them off (the chat line stays).
All art is original, painted locally for Backstage Forever.
After updating: quit WoW completely and start it again once. The game only picks up new art folders on a full restart, and /reload is not enough.

releases.title: Backstage Forever 0.39.1 — ask and answer in one window

changes.text: From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

One window for your questions. Click the owl on your minimap (or type /bf ask). The Backstage Forever panel opens over the top-right of your game with the cursor already in its question box. Type your question and press Enter, and the answer appears right under it. Ask a follow-up in the same box and it stacks underneath. Press Esc or click ✕ to close it, and your keyboard goes back to WoW.
The small question box that used to open inside the game is gone. WoW can't show answers from the app, so asking in game always meant two windows. Now the whole conversation happens in the panel.

While you're typing in the panel it stays open. Once you click back into the game, it hides by itself after the time you chose in Settings → Game connection. /bf ask your question from the chat line still works, and its answer appears in the same panel without taking your keyboard.
After updating: type /reload in WoW once.
From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

Know who's around. When an enemy player who can attack you becomes your target, passes under your mouse or shows a nameplate, Backstage Forever says so at the top of your screen: "Alliance level 32 Rogue nearby", or "Horde level ?? Warrior" when they're far above you. Chat gets their name and the zone. It works the same for Horde and Alliance players.

It stays quiet when it should. Each player alerts once and again only after five minutes out of sight. A group of five gives one alert, not five. Friendly players, players who can't attack you and battlegrounds or arenas never alert.

/bf enemy lists the last players you saw: name, faction, level, class, zone and how long ago. /bf enemy sound on adds a warning sound, /bf enemy off turns the alerts off and /bf enemy clear empties the list.
The addon only reads what the game already shows you. It never targets, marks or reports anyone, and it doesn't tell other players.
After updating: quit WoW and start it again once, because this version adds a new addon file. /reload isn't enough.

releases.title: Backstage Forever 0.41.0 — quality of life helpers

changes.text: From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.
Four small helpers. Each one is off until you switch it on, so nothing changes unless you want it to. Type /bf qol in WoW to see them.
Coordinates (/bf qol coords on): your map position, like "42.3, 67.8", just under the minimap.
Faster auto-loot (/bf qol loot on): when the game is auto-looting anyway, everything is taken at once instead of one item at a time. Items that ask "bind on pickup?" still wait for you.
Dismount at flight masters (/bf qol dismount on): when you open a flight master's map while mounted, you get off your mount so you can pick a flight. Never in combat.
Instant quest text (/bf qol questtext on): quest text appears at once instead of fading in, using the game's own setting. Switching it off puts your old setting back.
None of them accepts or hands in quests, picks a flight for you or loots anything the game wouldn't.
After updating: quit WoW and start it again once, because this version adds a new addon file.
From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

Quest together. When you're in a party with players who also run Backstage Forever, the addons quietly swap quest progress. Type /bf party to see each member's quests next to yours: "Raptor Thieves: them 5/8, you 2/8", plus the quests only they have, so you can ask them to share.

Shared waypoints. /bf party way sends your waypoint to the party (or where you're standing, if you haven't set one). The others see "Ann shares a waypoint: Kolkar camp at 40.0, 60.5" and can type /bf party go to put the arrow on it.
Only quest numbers and objective counts are sent, only to your party, and never in raids. /bf party off stops sending and listening.

releases.title: Backstage Forever 0.43.0 — all characters at a glance

changes.text: From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

Characters → All characters. Every character on one page: class portrait, level, how far through the level, rested XP, gold, free bag slots, professions, where they are and when you last played them. Click Switch to on a card to make that character the active one.

Rested XP keeps counting. The page works out how much rested XP each character has built up since you logged out: about 5% of a level every 8 hours in an inn or a city, a quarter of that elsewhere, up to 150%. From this version the addon remembers whether you logged out in a rested spot. Until each character has been saved once with 0.43, the page shows a range.

Who to play tonight. At the top, the page suggests a character and says why: "rested XP is full, so every hour away is wasted", "one level from 40 and riding", "not played for 20 days". It also warns when a character's bags are nearly full.
After updating: type /reload in WoW once on each character, so the addon saves the new rested flag.
From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.
Your next step, beside the game. On Now, click Mini Now. A small window opens and stays on top of your game. It shows one thing to do next:
a finished quest to hand in, and who to;
otherwise the nearest objective you still need, like "Raptor Head 3/12";
otherwise a quest to pick up nearby, or the zone to head for.

It also says which way to go from where you're standing ("south-east", "a short way north", "in The Barrens"). Under the step are your experience bar with rested XP and your pace this session: levels per hour and minutes to the next level.

Drag it by its top bar to wherever suits you, and close it with ✕. It never takes your keyboard away from the game. With the live link on it follows you as you play; without it, it shows your last save.
From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

Hear your next step. On Now, click Speak steps. From then on, whenever your next step changes, Backstage Forever reads it aloud with your computer's own Windows voice. For example: "Hand in Call of Water to Islen Waterseer, south-east", or "Raptor Thieves: Raptor Head 3/12, a short way north."
It's the same step that Mini Now shows: a quest to hand in first, then the nearest objective, then a quest to pick up. Say again repeats it. Click the button again to stop.
It's off until you switch it on, and the app remembers your choice. The voice runs on your computer, so nothing is sent anywhere. If Windows has no voice installed, the button tells you.

releases.title: Backstage Forever 0.46.0 — zones, replay and journey picture

changes.text: From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.

Adventure → Zones. Every zone you can level in, from 1 to 60, for your own faction (Horde and Alliance alike, plus the contested zones). Each zone is coloured by its level band and has a ring showing how many of its quests you've done, like "Durotar 18/22". A ★ marks zones you've finished (90% of their quests), a ◆ marks zones you've visited, and zones at your level have a gold edge. At the top, the page suggests the next zone worth clearing. Click any zone to open it on the World Map.
Replay your session. On the World Map, click ▶ to watch your path this session draw itself again on the zone you're looking at. Deaths and level-ups appear at the moment they happened.

Save a picture. Click 🖼 to save a hand-drawn-style picture of that path: the zone in sepia, your route in ink, where you started, died and levelled, with the zone name, your levels and time played. You choose where the PNG goes. It's made from your own path, with no game art beyond your own install's map.
The path is kept while the app is open, so a replay covers your current session.

releases.title: Backstage Forever 0.47.0 — plan tonight with the companion

changes.text: From Backstage Coding. Designed by Frank Arena.
"What should I do tonight?" Ask the companion and you get a plan in order. For example:
Empty your bags first: only 2 free slots.

Follow one step at a time, from level 1. In WoW, type /bf route guide. The scroll on your screen shows the next step on your race's route: pick up these quests, do this objective, hand in to this person, head to the next zone. The game's arrow points at the step, and the guide moves on by itself as you pick up and hand in quests.
/bf route skip skips the step you're on.
If you're well ahead of a step's level, the guide moves past it. If you're behind, it tells you.
Class quests show up as one step: "take the quest for your class, if they have one."

Human, Orc, Night Elf, Undead and Troll: levels 1 to about 42.
Tauren: 1 to 42, except levels 4 to 9.

✓ keeps it, marked as reviewed;
✗ leaves it out of the route;
↑ and ↓ move it earlier or later;
↺ undoes your change.

Your changes show in the app straight away and are saved on this computer. When you're happy with a route, click Export review. It saves a reviews.json file, and once that file is in the project the next release builds your review into the in-game guide (/bf route guide).

The Windows installer is timestamped and signed by Frank Arena through Azure Artifact Signing. Automated checks and isolated Windows packaging tests cover this build. Real WoW Forever validation is still in progress; report gameplay issues with the app/addon version and the steps to reproduce. Back up your journal before updating.

releases.title: Backstage Forever 1.9.0 — Badges and Classic raid tips

changes.text: Dungeon badges: earn First dungeon victory and Dungeon veteran from one or five distinct saved dungeon boss wins. Entering an instance, raid wins, and reference entries don’t count.

Quest-chain badges: three reviewed paths now have badges: The Defias Brotherhood (Westfall), A Husband’s Revenge, and The Missing Shipment. Every step must appear in the same character’s saved quest history.

Faction medals: earn separate Revered and Exalted medals for Stormwind, Orgrimmar, and Timbermaw Hold. A faction hidden during the latest scan cannot establish new medal progress; expand it in WoW and reload or log out to save a fresh observation. The new badges and medals are desktop-only.
Classic raid tips: reviewed Molten Core and Blackwing Lair boss tips are available in the desktop Instance Atlas and in-game with /bf boss. These are reference notes, not live encounter validation.

Journal compatibility: reputation scans saved in the same second are kept in order. Back up your journal before rolling back to v1.8.0: ordinary saves there preserve the newer awards, but accepting a newer game snapshot in v1.8.0 can lose them. See the rollback and recovery guide.

Pick up where you left off. Now shows one next action and why it was suggested; the in-game Adventure Compass keeps recommendations quieter. Desktop Quiet, Leveling, and Workshop presets preview changes before applying them. Addon setup gives specific recovery steps and supports a clean retry.

Recover a route. Desktop Guided Route supports resuming, skipping without granting completion, and opening a matching map target when evidence allows it. Character switches, deletion, and local reset clear the appropriate route or recommendation state. The Dwarf/Gnome opening and Horde Desolace reviews record exclusions; this is not a new or verified 1–60 route.

Prepare from saved evidence. Workshop separates carried shortfalls from last-seen storage and conditional purchase estimates. Ledger shows saved carried materials for supported reputation turn-ins. These are not live stock, prices or purchase instructions.

Review your dungeons and gear. Instance Atlas links supported loot to the same item in Character Sheet and distinguishes observed ownership from reference information. Journey shows retained personal dungeon defeats, not complete lifetime totals, clears, or lockouts. Classic Zul’Gurub boss tips are reviewed references, not live mechanics qualification.
Ask about saved Workshop materials offline. Supported questions can be answered without a model or provider; the offline exchange is excluded from later provider history and memory reuse.

Platform and sharing limits. macOS reports saved-only operation; native screen capture is not shipped or qualified. Quest-giver qualification is local groundwork only: no new sharing transport, consent defaults or server deployment. Live WoW, native Mac, and an installed Windows update/rollback are not certified by automated fixtures.

releases.title: Backstage Forever 1.11.0 — Dungeon preparation, savings goals, and quest-chain progress

changes.text: Prepare for a dungeon offline. Ask the desktop Companion Dungeon prep for The Deadmines? using a supported Atlas name or exact #ID. No model or account is needed. With active-character context enabled, the answer can show possible matches in the saved quest log and starred loot references compatible with the saved build. This is not proof of quest eligibility, personal drops, clears, lockouts, or live mechanics. The exchange is excluded from provider history and cannot be saved to Companion Memory.

Workshop and dungeon questions are desktop-only in 1.11. In-game Ask Panel submissions and /bf ask questions about these features direct you to the desktop without reading saved preparation data or calling a provider. Choose Open in app, then ask again in Companion with Use my active character enabled if you want saved-character details. Other in-game questions work as before.

Turn a Workshop estimate into a savings goal. Review a priced estimate before setting or replacing the Ledger goal. An unpriced batch cannot set a goal. Switching characters or changing the goal while a review is open makes the old confirmation ineligible. The estimate is not a current market price or a purchase instruction.

See progress on reviewed quest chains. Unfinished quest-chain badges show completed steps from the saved character and the remaining reviewed steps when evidence is available. Progress does not award the badge early or establish quest eligibility.

Catch up after an update. The illustrated Field Dispatch covers the releases you skipped when the app knows your previous installed version. Choose Not now to defer it or Got it to acknowledge it. A fresh install or an unknown predecessor does not claim an upgrade range.
Find past changes in Settings. Open Settings → Updates → What’s New to search the bundled release history offline, even after dismissing the recap.

Recognized dungeon and raid preparation questions stay offline. Ask desktop Companion a question such as Dungeon prep for The Deadmines?. The reply uses eligible World of Warcraft: Forever evidence and identifies gaps rather than filling them with facts from another edition. Saved-character context is optional. These exchanges are not sent to a model or reused in provider history or Companion Memory.

Know what this covers. Saved preparation still belongs in desktop Companion, not the in-game Ask Panel. This change does not qualify general Companion Q&A as Forever evidence. Atlas remains a separately labeled reference, not a substitute for verified Forever facts.

releases.title: Backstage Forever 1.12.1 — Forever dungeon and raid questions

changes.text: Recognized dungeon and raid fact questions stay local. Ask Companion Where is #dm? or What bosses are in Scarlet Monastery?. If there is no verified current Forever answer, it says so rather than using Classic Atlas facts or asking a model. Atlas remains a separate reference.

Travel keeps the destination separate from the starting point. A dungeon named as the origin is not treated as the destination, and an unresolved explicit origin does not silently fall back to your character’s location.

Historical observations are not a current boss list. Historical encounters for #sm and Historical encounters for #rfk label the Forever build and collection window. These are not proof of access or of your character’s defeats.

Try four offline drills in Adventure → Practice Lab. Practice an opener, resource pooling, defensive timing and heal targeting. Each choice gives a simulated result and a tip. No game, character import, account or provider is needed; the scenarios are fictional and attempts are not saved.

Try the Frost Mage pilot in Characters → Talents. The solo, single-target guide is available for an imported active Frost Mage at levels 23–25 on WoW Forever build 1.60.1.70959, after you confirm Frostbolt Rank 4 and Ice Lance Rank 1 in your spellbook. This is offline teaching, not live rotation advice or spellbook detection. Your confirmations are not saved.

Open the Dungeon Fieldbook in Adventure → Dungeons & raids → The Deadmines. Before the run, review the approximate entrance, quest records, manual preparation checks and the active character’s wish list for this dungeon. Inside, three boss cues are labeled Classic reference, not verified Forever mechanics. Afterward, see dated defeats from the active character’s saved Journal. This is not a run, lockout or personal-loot tracker; other dungeons keep the standard Atlas details.

Plan a guild run in Plans → Party → Guild Run Pack. Preview an event with its organizer time zone, meeting point, roles and preparation checklist. Save it locally, then export a JSON pack or plain-text copy to share yourself. Recipients can review a pack before saving it, apply later revisions or cancellations, and keep their own preparation checks private. There is no account, RSVP collection, automatic delivery or sync.

Delete all local data removes leftover private staging files. Reset now clears temporary files left by interrupted journal, credential, or recovery-preference writes. If one of those files is blocked, reset stops before changing the saved journal or credentials so you can retry. Unrelated files and exports are left alone.

See alternate tasks beside your next step in Now. Open saved quest markers in the Map and return to the same quest in Quest Guide. Map cards now explain which pins are saved observations and which areas are approximate reference.

Prepare for The Deadmines in the Dungeon Fieldbook, review saved defeats, and try the fictional opener in Practice Lab. Open an editable Companion draft without sending it. The Atlas has improved keyboard navigation and German layouts.

Review supplies, inspect Workshop material needs and compare gear in Sheet. Supply Desk commitments are session-only. Expanded recipe chains and local craft handoffs are not included: saved recipes can carry over from a different client build.
Try the reviewed tank and healer lessons and the manual spellbook checks in Academy. Data Coverage explains which guidance has been reviewed for the selected character’s saved build.

Review organizer notes and debrief decisions locally, and separately preview the welcome text you choose to copy. Review a local Deadmines plan pack before importing it. Private organizer notes and decisions are not included in portable Guild Run Packs.
Use private weekly and after-action notes to review saved observations. Notes entered there are session-only; they do not appear in shared recaps or backups.

This desktop-first update does not add new native Compass commands or expand Companion quest pickup and turn-in coverage. Classic reference, fictional drills and saved observations are not live WoW Forever verification.

Track a watched quest in Adventure Compass, check missing objectives, and review a nearby hand-in when the game confirms it is ready. If objective data is unreadable or incomplete, Compass withholds the hand-in tip and its waypoint. Eligible detours and waypoints still require your action. Reviewed objective hints use exact quest and target matches.

Gathering map marks show approximate, recent last-seen Copper Vein and Silverleaf spots on Forever build 1.60.1.70862 when your current gathering skill is verified. The separate /bf nodes command lists remembered spots. Supported quest reward comparisons and a narrow Mage Frostbolt rank reminder do not select rewards, equip items, cast spells or change action slots for you.

Use /bf helpers panel to change eleven per-character preferences in WoW. In desktop Settings → Game connection → In-Game Helpers, open Prepare changes for WoW to draft only the choices you want to change. Verify the character logged into WoW before pasting the whole command outside combat. The desktop neither applies nor verifies it. Quest-item sale protection remains independent of the optional helpers.

Helpers depend on the game data available to the addon. A last-seen spot is not a live spawn, and a missing hint does not prove there is nothing nearby. This update does not add general DPS coaching or expand Companion quest or Workshop recipe-chain advice.
